The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

Coldcard ships firmware after $114 million bitcoin theft; says AI helped catch more bugs. Three weeks of review turned up problems unrelated to the flaw that cost users $114 million, but updating still does not make a compromised wallet safe. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Analysts split on whether Bitcoin's surge past key levels signals a new bull run. Market watchers say sudden sharp price spikes and forced short liquidations are the classic signs of a bottom, though macro risks still remain. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

The hard truth is that the Clarity Act is an anti-crypto bill. After years of stalled bills, misguided enforcement, and catastrophic collapses, almost any comprehensive crypto legislation began to look like progress. But Clarity is turning that hunger for progress into a political trap, argues Berkeley Law lecturer Hermine Wong. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Bitcoin faces $80,000 test as thinner weekend liquidity looms. Your day-ahead look for Aug. 21, 2026 Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Nomura-backed Laser Digital wins Japan's first crypto approval in four years. Laser Digital Japan will offer liquidity to domestic crypto providers, with institutional trading services planned to follow as the appetite for crypto in Japan grows. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Bitcoin tops $77,000 as best week since 2023 pulls altcoins along for the ride. BTC has gained 24% since Monday and reached the level implied by its inverse head-and-shoulders break, with shorts still taking a contrarian position. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $76,795 with a +7.09% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $2,376.98 with a +4.21% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

The Stablecoin Statement specifically addresses stablecoins that are designed to maintain a stable value relative to the US dollar (USD) on a one-for-one basis, [...] On September 19, 2025, Treasury issued an Advance Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (ANPRM), seeking public comment related to its implementation of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins (GENIUS) Act, a comprehensive framework for the federal regulation of payment stablecoins enacted on July 18, 2025.

Read more on Latham's Global Fintech & Digital Assets Blog. items.title: Cryptocurrency Regulation: A Guide to U.S. & Global Policies
items.description:
Cryptocurrency regulation in the United States has historically been fragmented, with federal agencies applying different interpretations based on the nature and use of each asset. That splintered approach began to change in 2025, when Congress passed legislation to establish a clearer framework for stablecoins and digital asset markets.

## Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs [...] Cryptocurrency regulation is no longer a theoretical debate—it’s an evolving framework that is beginning to take shape worldwide. In the United States, Congress made progress in 2025 toward establishing federal oversight of stablecoins and digital asset markets. One measure—the GENIUS Act—was signed into law. [...] In the U.S., landmark legislation enacted in July 2025 has begun defining the roles of federal agencies in regulating stablecoins and digital commodities. Although implementation is ongoing, these laws represent a shift away from case-by-case enforcement and toward a structured national policy.
